code.note: Shell archive, not a plain source file: read the text, do not execute it. It holds Doc/makefile, Drivers/Dp (driver.f = DRDFRENL, double precision; RES = its reference output), Drivers/Sp (single precision), and Src/Dp (dfrenl.f, dcspxx.f, dcospx.f, and the helpers). Drivers/Dp/RES is the shipped reference the rerun compares against.

field: numerics (special functions: Fresnel integrals C, S, f, g)

claim.location: Shipped double-precision reference output Drivers/Dp/RES, row X = 1.0000000E+00 (the demonstration driver DRDFRENL prints C(x), S(x), g(x), f(x) at X = 0.5*I for I = -12..12; X = 1.0 is I = 2). Claim value: C(1.0) = 7.7989340E-01 in the C(x) column.

reference.sha256: not computed; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.metric: C(x), the Fresnel cosine integral C(x) = integral from 0 to x of cos(pi t^2/2) dt, at x = 1.0, as printed by the double-precision driver DRDFRENL (format 1p5e15.07).
claim.paper_value: Shipped reference value 7.7989340E-01 (C(1.0), Drivers/Dp/RES). Article text not read.

values.name: C(1.0), Fresnel cosine integral, double precision

tolerance.basis: The reference prints 8 significant digits (7 after the point in exponent form), so printed rounding is about 5e-8 absolute; 1e-6 absolute covers that and compiler/libm rounding, and still catches a wrong algorithm (the single-precision RES differs from the double-precision one only at the 7th digit). Fixed now, before any run; not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: the driver evaluates 25 points.
cost.data_size: None: values are computed from X in the driver.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The double-precision driver evaluates the Fresnel integrals at fixed points and the shipped reference prints the values, so a rerun must run the routines to reproduce C(1.0); the value is not a closed form.
